s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive extraocular muscle limitation with a localized orbital mass
salient_findings: Slowly developing limitation in right-eye movement
Restricted abduction of the right eye
Extraconal mass at the right superolateral orbital wall with smooth bone remodeling
key_facts: 5-year-old boy with no prior medical history
No pain, inflammation, fever, trauma, or history of ocular infection
Overall health unchanged
Abduction of the right eye was restricted
No signs of proptosis, strabismus, visual impairment, or inflammation in either eye
Laboratory studies, including an infectious work-up, were negative
Noncontrast CT showed a well-circumscribed extraconal mass
MRI demonstrated a cystic mass in the right superior extraconal compartment
Mild compression on the external and superior rectus muscles
No involvement of the optic nerve, intraconal fat, or intracranial extension

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a well-circumscribed extraconal mass with smooth bone remodeling and fluid-attenuating content

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to dermoid cyst, could explain the cystic mass in the right superior extraconal compartment

shortlist.label: Orbital lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Could cause a cystic mass with mild compression on surrounding muscles

shortlist.label: Cavernous hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign orbital tumor that could present as a well-circumscribed extraconal mass

shortlist.label: Mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the fluid-attenuating content and smooth bone remodeling of the mass

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-circumscribed extraconal mass with smooth bone remodeling and fluid-attenuating content on CT, along with the cystic appearance on MRI that is hyperintense on T2-weighted images and hypointense on FLAIR imaging, is consistent with a dermoid cyst. The lack of enhancement after gadolinium administration and the absence of aggressive features such as bone invasion or significant compression of vital structures also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: While similar to dermoid cysts, epidermoid cysts are less common in the orbit and typically do not contain the same variety of tissue elements, making dermoid cyst a more likely diagnosis given the imaging characteristics.

rejected.label: Orbital lymphangioma
rejected.why: Lymphangiomas are typically more infiltrative and less well-circumscribed than the described lesion, and often involve the intraconal space, which is not the case here.

rejected.label: Cavernous hemangioma
rejected.why: Cavernous hemangiomas are usually more heterogeneous on imaging due to the presence of blood-filled spaces and often show more pronounced enhancement after contrast administration, which does not match the described imaging findings.

rejected.label: Mucocele
rejected.why: Mucoceles are typically associated with the paranasal sinuses and would be expected to show signs of sinus involvement or erosion, which are not mentioned in the case description.
